item.title: ‘Don’t have to do this’: Trump tells new press secy Zacharia she can quit if she wants
item.description: Katie Zacharia has faced significant scrutiny after her brief tenure as White House press secretary. Donald Trump expressed concerns about the job's challenges and suggested she reconsider her position. The media has provided harsh coverage of her professional background and recent press briefing. Despite his doubts, Trump emphasized that the decision about her future is ultimately up to her.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Russia strikes 9 Ukrainian regions as new report shows spike in civilian casualties
item.description: Russia's recent strikes have plunged Ukraine into darkness, impacting electricity for hundreds of thousands and resulting in civilian injuries. Amidst this turmoil, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy voiced his worries over diminishing US support during a summit in Brussels. Civilian casualties surged by 85% in September compared to last year, as Ukraine urgently calls for more military aid while the EU seeks to enhance its support for the beleaguered nation.

item.title: Off-duty US soldier saves gunshot victim, earns Army Commendation Medal for quick first aid
item.description: When gunfire erupted near his residence, Private First Class Stephen Bradley sprang into action, showcasing his military training to help a gunshot victim. His quick thinking involved applying a tourniquet and pressure dressing, stabilizing the civilian's injuries until emergency responders arrived. Local authorities are actively investigating the shooting, while Bradley's bravery earned him the Army Commendation Medal for his commendable response during this critical situation.

item.title: Zelenskyy slams Trump's diesel deal, says will help fund Putin’s war in Ukraine
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concerns over the US diesel deal with Russia. He warned that this agreement could provide additional funds for Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine. Zelenskyy emphasized the need for Europe to increase support to Ukraine as missile attacks continue. The president requested significant financial assistance to maintain Ukraine's defense against Russian aggression.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Putin, Trump to announce several joint projects as Russian diesel returns to market
item.description: Russia and the United States are set to announce new initiatives beyond their recent diesel agreement. Discussions reportedly include collaborative data centre projects powered by Russian nuclear energy. Supplies of diesel have begun reaching international markets following the deal with the United States. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has criticized the arrangement, expressing concerns about its implications for energy revenue.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: US temple plot, school shooting: Gun epidemic spares no one as debate goes off target
item.description: A neo-Nazi teen attempted a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois, but his rifle jammed. The attack highlights ongoing debates about gun violence and societal issues, including parenting and mental health. Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi expressed horror that the attack targeted Indian Americans during worship. Many lawmakers condemned the incident, emphasizing the need to address religious and racial hatred in society.
item.dc:creator: Chidanand Rajghatta

item.title: Dolly Parton donated $100,000 for a healing garden at a hospital tied to her family roots
item.description: A new $55 million medical facility has opened in South Carolina, featuring an outdoor healing garden. This garden was funded by a $100,000 donation from country music star Dolly Parton, honoring her family's local roots. The garden aims to provide patients and their families a peaceful retreat during difficult times. Parton expressed her support for the hospital staff and future patients during the opening ceremony.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mailchimp’s founders turned a side project into a $12 billion business without outside funding
item.description: Originating from humble beginnings, Mailchimp evolved within two decades from a small business tool to a powerhouse in the marketing industry. Launched by The Rocket Science Group's Ben Chestnut and Dan Kurzius, it caught the attention of Intuit, who acquired it for around $12 billion in 2021. With a sharp focus on customer-centric innovation and maintaining independence, Mailchimp solidified its status as a leader in global digital marketing.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California wildfires spread amid strong winds; over 150,000 customers without power
item.description: Southern California is currently grappling with wildfires, prompting evacuation orders in several communities and causing widespread power outages. The combination of heat and dryness has amplified fire risks, with strong winds anticipated. Firefighters are actively battling flames in areas like Malibu and Azusa, urging locals to stay alert. In an effort to mitigate fire hazards, precautionary power outages have been instituted across numerous regions.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: 'OH'IO No: Vivek Ramaswamy's Catch-22 problem with MAGA
item.description: Ramaswamy is running to become Ohio governor, a position he perhaps sees as a stepping stone to something bigger in the party. Yet Ramaswamy’s association with Trump is increasingly becoming a liability among neutral voters, while his faith and skin colour are proving a deterrent among parts of the MAGA base.
item.dc:creator: Nirmalya Dutta

item.title: 'We'll knock it out fast': Trump may target Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility
item.description: Donald Trump indicated that the US may target Iran's Pickaxe Mountain facility to deter nuclear weapon development. He stated that nuclear weapons would not be necessary for achieving US objectives in the situation. The remarks followed ongoing US-Israeli strikes against Iran since February, amid rising tensions. Iran's foreign ministry denied any nuclear activity at the site, labeling US threats as baseless.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Russian officer helped Ukraine kill over 300 troops by leaking military secrets
item.description: Russian army lieutenant Lev Stupnikov took a perilous stand against his own military by secretly supplying Ukrainian forces with critical intelligence. His actions led to the targeted elimination of more than 300 Russian soldiers and deliberate sabotage of weapons systems, culminating in his flight to the Russian Volunteer Corps as a direct challenge to Putin's leadership. Stupnikov’s bravery reshaped the landscape of the ongoing Ukraine conflict.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh
